A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoBencher, with matching capability experiments and search procedures despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark-generation experiments, model accuracies and rankings, an adaptive-search ablation, and a human dataset-construction study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds safety evaluations, human quality judgments, variance analyses and further ablations.

M1.justification: The proposal, generation, feedback and reranking procedure is retained. v2 adds a safety adaptation: generate harmful requests without privileged information, treat abstention as the correct response, filter for harmfulness and optimize attack success rate instead of the capability objective (Sections 3.2 and 4.1). This modifies the existing procedure without replacing its search mechanism.

E1.justification: The five original capability domains remain. v2 adds safety evaluation through generated harmful-request datasets, HarmBench and XSTest, including unsafe-only and mixed safe/unsafe evaluation. Appendix O also describes easier and harder safety datasets constructed against different model groups. This substantially extends the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: The original HumanBench comparisons and adaptive-search ablation remain. v2 adds reported safety comparisons against XSTest, HarmBench and HarmBench GCG-T in Table 1; Table 12 provides model-level comparisons with HarmBench Zero Shot and both XSTest variants. LM-Examiner is discussed as related work, rather than established as an experimentally evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces safety searches with 10 iterations, 10 descriptions per iteration and 10 examples per description; the capability settings remain 8, 5 and 50. It adds evaluator/temperature experiments and human correctness, salience and harmfulness protocols, including two judgments per safety prompt and filtering thresholds. The retained human robustness study changes its stated annotator from an author in v1 Section 6.3 to Mechanical Turk workers in v2 Appendix J.4, despite identical results; the PDFs do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: The adaptive-search ablation, human reconstruction study, search trajectories and separation/headroom analysis are retained. v2 adds removal of privileged information, alternative evaluator models, temperature sensitivity, seed and dataset-size analyses, direct human audits of correctness/salience/harmfulness, and safety failure analyses (Appendices G–J and O). These test several previously unexamined sources of reliability and failure.

E5.justification: v1 already reports plus/minus values for novelty but provides little uncertainty methodology. v2 adds comparisons among three seed-labeled generations, standard deviations versus dataset size for all three capability metrics, and uncertainty values for all three metrics in the temperature-1 experiment (Figure 3 and Tables 3–4). These are new uncertainty analyses, not evidence of increased repetitions for the retained headline results.

E6.justification: The original capability scores and ranking/accuracy tables are retained, including v1 Tables 4–6 becoming v2 Tables 9–11. New results include safety ASR of 0.38 versus 0.08 for XSTest, 0.28 for HarmBench and 0.45 for HarmBench GCG-T (v2 Table 1), plus ablation and human-audit outcomes. Table 6 reports correctness of 92.8–97.0%; Section 6.4 interchanges the history and science error rates relative to that table. These are additional findings, not improved scores on the retained experiments.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal harmfulness and rejection-based ASR definitions and a constrained safety objective. It also substantively changes the printed novelty regression: v1 minimizes over w, whereas v2 jointly optimizes theta and a stated M-dimensional bias b. As written, theta=0 and b=v_c fit any target exactly, making novelty zero for nonconstant accuracy vectors. This affects a central mathematical definition, although it does not establish an implementation change.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on constructing salient, novel and difficult capability benchmarks, leaving safety to future work. v2 claims a declarative framework demonstrated under both capability and safety objectives, with systematic safety vulnerabilities becoming a main contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. The original capability novelty and difficulty claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of privileged-information ablations, temperature/evaluator robustness and safety failure mechanisms. It attributes relatively strong Llama safety performance to its absence from the original search targets and distinguishes systematic category discovery from request-specific attacks. Appendix A adds a low-resource translation limitation and expands the discussion of evaluator-family bias and necessary human checks; Appendix E discusses other forms of evaluator advantage.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents generation temperature, objective weights, the 500K-view salience threshold, candidate decoding and judge prompting, final dataset sizes, annotation procedures, and vLLM/A100 runtime and cost information. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained capability runs. Conversely, v1's asset-license appendix, explicit MIT release statement and lexical-overlap verification sentence disappear. The code URL still identifies the same repository.

R1.justification: The closest-work discussion shifts from TreeEval to LM-Examiner, emphasizing privileged information as the distinction. v2 expands positioning around automated dataset construction and systematic safety failures, adding discussion of BIG-Bench, lm-evaluation-harness, GCG, AutoDAN and safety benchmarks. It removes the earlier Inverse Scaling case study and several citations supporting the original capability-correlation motivation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around declarative construction. Terminology shifts from topics and generator/test-taker models to dataset descriptions and evaluator/candidate models. The framework is divided into capability and safety settings, metric-attribution prose is integrated into the search explanation, and experimental material and appendices are extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 extends Table 1 with safety comparisons, rebuilds the qualitative-example table, and adds displays for variance, ablations, human judgments and safety results, including an annotation-guideline figure. Existing human-study and ranking tables are relocated, while trajectory, histogram and frontier figures are retained and resized. Conference formatting also substantially changes table placement and page layout.

improvement.justification: The added human quality audits, variance analysis and component/evaluator ablations strengthen validation beyond v1's human reconstruction study, while safety experiments demonstrate broader applicability. The net gain is limited by the unexplained annotator change with identical study results, inconsistent correctness summaries, and the degenerate bias specification in the revised novelty regression. These issues weaken the clarity and reproducibility of otherwise useful additions.
